capability: Automatic soft-edge blend between overlapping projectors
what_it_does: Select two or more overlapping quads and press one button; MadMapper works out the shared area and fades each projector's edge so the seam disappears. Width and a gamma value are then tuned per edge. Angled overlaps are handled with a feathered mask inside each surface.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'soft edge', 'edge blend' and 'feather': no hits anywhere. 'keystone': no hits. jit.gl.cornerpin's refpage describes repositioning four image corners only. A blend ramp could be written by hand as a shader in jit.gl.slab or jit.gl.pix, but nothing computes the overlap.
notes: The automatic overlap calculation is the part with no Max equivalent; the ramp itself is a simple shader.

capability: Mesh warping with free points, Bézier handles and a linked input mesh
what_it_does: A quad gets an internal grid of warp points that are added anywhere, dragged on the output, and given Bézier tangent handles for curved surfaces. By default each point moved on the output is mirrored on the input side so the picture is not stretched; the link can be turned off to edit the two meshes separately.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'warp': no object; three jitter userguide topics mention it. 'bezier': only jit.mgraphics text. jit.gl.cornerpin (refpage: maps a texture by repositioning the image corners, with mouse handles in the window) covers four corners. jit.gl.nurbs (refpage: renders a NURBS surface from a control matrix) and jit.gl.mesh (geometry from matrices) can hold a warped surface, but neither gives draggable warp points on the output.
notes: A Max user would have to build the point editor. jit.gl.nurbs's refpage lists a 'ctlshow' attribute; whether its control points can be dragged with the mouse was not checked.

capability: Layer list of surfaces, each with an input crop and an output shape edited by dragging
what_it_does: The whole mapping is a stack of surfaces. For each one you drag a rectangle over the source to choose what it shows, and separately drag its corners on the output to place it. List order is drawing order; groups scale their children's opacity.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'cornerpin' finds jit.gl.cornerpin and jit.world (which the refpage says contains a jit.gl.cornerpin, enabled with 'enable_cornerpin'). jit.gl.videoplane's refpage: shows video in OpenGL. jit.gl.handle's refpage: turns mouse drags into rotate and position messages. One jit.gl.cornerpin per surface is the Max way; there is no surface list, no input-crop view and no grouping.
notes: This is MadMapper's whole interface, so it is a design difference more than a missing object. Listed because it is what the other mapping candidates sit on.

capability: Bézier masks with feathering that follow the surface or the source
what_it_does: Masks are drawn on the output freehand or point by point and smoothed into Bézier curves. A surface can carry several, each inverted or not, each with a feathered edge. A mask can stay fixed, follow the surface's warp, or follow the input picture. A separate Mask surface cuts every layer beneath it.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'mask': jit.keyscreen (refpage: a three-source chromakey that builds a mask from a key image) and av.pix.mask (package entry: makes a black/white mask from an image). 'feather': no hits. jit.mgraphics has curve_to, fill and path methods in its refpage, so a mask texture can be drawn from code. Nothing provides drawing a mask on the output with the mouse.

capability: 3D calibration: line up a 3D model with a real object from matched points
what_it_does: Import an OBJ of the real object, pick known points on the model, and place each on the matching point of the object as the projector sees it. MadMapper solves the projector's view, shows the RMS error as points are added, and locks the result.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'calibrat': nothing in Max itself. Package hits: cv.jit.calibration (camera intrinsics and lens distortion from chessboard views), cv.jit.findchessboardcorners, cv.jit.unproject (2D image points to 3D camera coordinates). jit.gl.model's refpage: reads and draws OBJ and other formats. None solves a projector pose from point pairs on a model.
notes: The cv.jit objects calibrate a camera, not a projector. Whether they could be combined to do this was not tested.

capability: Structured-light scan that gives the projector's own view of the scene
what_it_does: The projector shows a series of stripe patterns while a camera photographs them. The result is an image of the scene as seen from the projector, pixel for pixel, set as the output's background so surfaces can be drawn on it away from the site.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'structured light': no hits anywhere. jit.grab's refpage: digitizes video from any digitizer. Capture exists; the pattern projection and decoding do not.

capability: Camera scan that finds where every LED pixel is
tool_names: Map LEDs at 0,0 if not detected
what_it_does: MadMapper flashes each LED in a DMX range one at a time while a camera watches, then places the fixtures in the workspace where the camera saw them. An irregular LED installation is mapped without measuring.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). No DMX output objects in Max to begin with (see the DMX candidates). 'pixel map' and 'fixture': no relevant hits.

capability: Camera scan that calibrates a laser to the scene
what_it_does: The laser draws a moving 16 x 16 grid of dots while a camera records them. The result is a background image for the laser output showing the scene from the laser's position, for aligning paths to real objects.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'laser', 'ilda', 'galvo': no hits in Max; one package hit, Vsynth's vector_3ch_out (see the laser output candidate).

capability: Line surfaces: paths drawn on the output with media running along them
what_it_does: Paths are drawn on the output freehand or point by point, with thickness, joins and Bézier curves, to trace edges of architecture or LED strips. A media item is mapped along the path, either per segment, chained over all paths, or by the paths' position on the output, so a pattern can run along an outline.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). jit.gl.path's refpage: generates and renders a 3D path as a line, ribbon, tube or extruded contour, storing position, colour, scale and orientation per point; attributes include 'joinstyle' and 'interpmode', and messages 'append', 'edit', 'edithandle'. That covers rendering a path. Drawing it on the output with the mouse and mapping a texture along it were not found.
notes: The four texturing mode names come from the MadLaser guide's Laser Lines section; the release notes name 'Match Output Geometry' for video lines too.

capability: SVG files become editable line surfaces, laser paths or fixtures
what_it_does: Dropping an SVG into a project turns its paths into Line surfaces that can then be edited and animated. The same file can become laser paths or DMX fixtures. Masks and lines can be exported back to SVG.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'svg': no object by that name. jit.mgraphics's refpage lists svg_create, svg_render, svg_set, svg_get_size, so Max can draw an SVG into a picture. Nothing found that reads an SVG's paths as points for jit.gl.path or similar.

capability: Video wall layout built from panel count, resolution and bezel size
what_it_does: A template asks how many screens across and down, their resolution, the bezel width and their rotation, and creates the grid of surfaces with the bezel gaps allowed for. An output's destination can also split one canvas across several displays.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). jit.displays's refpage: enumerates and sets monitor attributes. jit.window: draws to a window, with 'rect', 'pos', 'fullscreen'. No bezel or video-wall helper found.
notes: Simple arithmetic to build by hand; listed because it is a one-step setup in MadMapper.

capability: Alignment aids drawn on the real output
what_it_does: Each output can show a test pattern, the mouse position as a cross or circle on the projected image (or as a laser beam), the names and outlines of selected surfaces, or only the surfaces being edited. These make it possible to work while looking at the real object instead of the screen.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). jit.gl.cornerpin's refpage has 'drawcorners', 'corner_color', 'hover' attributes, so its handles are visible in the output window. No ready test pattern or output cursor was found; both can be drawn with jit.gl.sketch or jit.gl.text.

capability: DMX fixtures as surfaces that sample the picture under them
what_it_does: A light fixture is placed on the output like a video surface and takes its colour from the pixels beneath it, so any video composition drives LEDs and lights directly. Sampling can be one pixel, a box average, or a stretched average for strips, and each fixture has a response curve.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'dmx': no Max object; the word appears once, in the serial refpage. One package hit: fxwdmxusbpro (an abstraction that sends a list of channel values to an Enttec DMX USB Pro over serial). 'fixture', 'pixel map': nothing. A Max user would read pixels from a jit.matrix and build the channel list by hand.

capability: Art-Net and sACN in and out, with node discovery and many universes
what_it_does: MadMapper sends and receives DMX over Ethernet as Art-Net or sACN, in broadcast or unicast, finds Art-Net nodes by polling, and handles thousands of universes. Incoming DMX can control any parameter. Small modules route universes to USB interfaces, forward a universe as OSC, and show live channel values.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'art-net', 'artnet', 'sacn', 'e131': no hits in Max or in the package library. udpsend and udpreceive (refpages: send and receive messages over UDP) are the only transport; the packet format would have to be built by hand.
notes: Third-party Art-Net externals for Max may exist outside this machine; none is in the repo's package library.

capability: Fixture definitions: channel types, 16-bit pairs, computed channels, wiring order
what_it_does: A fixture type is described once: its pixel grid, the meaning of each channel (colour components, generic sliders, or a value computed by a GLSL expression from colour, position, time and other sliders), 8 or 16 bits, and which of 16 wiring orders its pixels follow. Definitions are files that can be shared. Moving heads use colour channels fed by video and slider channels for pan, tilt and gobo.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'fixture': no hits anywhere.

capability: Fixture layouts imported from and exported to SVG or CSV, patch included
what_it_does: A lighting layout drawn in a vector program becomes patched fixtures on import: universe, channel, fixture type and strip length are read from each shape's id or attributes, and layer groups become fixture groups. Exporting gives an SVG that rebuilds the same setup or serves as a guide for making video.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). No fixture concept in Max, so nothing to import into.

capability: Record DMX streams with synced audio and play them back
what_it_does: Records every DMX frame MadMapper sends, or that arrives from another desk, into a compact sequence file with an optional audio track kept in sync. Sequences are replayed by a player module, placed in timelines, or exported to a standalone player.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). mtr's refpage: records messages and plays them back in sequence, with read and write. It could record channel lists as messages, but there is no DMX-specific recorder and no stored-changes-only file format.

capability: Laser output to ILDA DACs, including over audio channels
what_it_does: Drives laser projectors directly: coloured paths are turned into frames of points and sent to network or USB DACs, or as five audio channels (X, Y, R, G, B) to an AVB or Dante audio interface. Any number of lasers can be used.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'ilda', 'etherdream', 'galvo': no hits anywhere. 'laser': one package hit, Vsynth's vector_3ch_out (package entry: sends vector X, Y and brightness signals to audio outputs). That is the same idea as MadMapper's audio laser output, without colour channels or any DAC protocol.
notes: The audio route is the one a Max patch could plausibly follow, since X/Y/R/G/B as signals is ordinary MSP. Whether vector_3ch_out is meant for lasers or for oscilloscopes was not checked.

capability: Laser path planning: blanking, corner dwell, speed, draw order, frame rate
what_it_does: Before points go to the laser, MadMapper orders the paths to shorten beam travel, shares scan time between paths by length, adds points at corners so they stay sharp, blanks the beam between paths, shifts colours in time to match the mirrors, and either holds the frame rate or holds the detail when there is too much to draw.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). No laser objects in Max or the package library, so none of this exists.
notes: This is the part that would be hardest to rebuild; it encodes what real scanners can physically do.

capability: Trace video into laser paths in real time
what_it_does: A movie, image or camera feed is traced every frame on the GPU, either by thinning bright lines to their skeleton or by edge detection. Paths can be filtered by length and capped in number, and the tracing stages can be previewed.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'vectoriz': nothing relevant. 'contour': cv.jit.findcontours (package entry: traces contours from a binary image as ordered point sequences) and cv.jit.canny (Canny edge detection to 1-pixel binary edges). These run on matrices on the CPU. The line-skeleton mode and the length filtering were not found.
notes: jit.sobel's refpage: Sobel and Prewitt gradient edge detection on matrices.

capability: Shaders that output coloured paths instead of pixels
what_it_does: A laser material is a GLSL function called once per sample point that returns a 2D position, a colour and a shape number; a change of shape number starts a new path. The previous frame's points can be read back for motion that depends on the past. A small library adds move-to, line-to and curve-to calls.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). No laser-specific object. The mechanism itself (a shader writing positions and colours into a small texture, one row each) could be done with jit.gl.slab (refpage: generate and process images with fragment shaders) or jit.gl.pix, then read back; nothing interprets such a texture as paths.
notes: Status is 'partial' only because the texture trick is available in Max; the path interpretation and laser output are absent.

capability: Split one laser composition across several lasers
what_it_does: A laser composition built on an output with no hardware is looped back as media and shared out between several real lasers, so a picture too complex for one scanner stays bright and steady. Shapes are tracked from frame to frame so each stays on the same laser. The looped composition can also be mesh warped as a whole.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). No laser objects in Max or the package library.

capability: Laser safety limits built into the output
what_it_does: Each laser output has masks the beam cannot enter, or enters only at reduced power, and a limit on the power of a beam that is not moving. Lasers emit nothing until armed and are un-armed when the computer wakes from sleep.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). No laser objects in Max or the package library.
notes: The manual itself says software masks must not be the only protection.

capability: ILDA files: import, export and recording
what_it_does: Standard .ild laser files play as media on laser surfaces. Any laser output can save its current frame or record a movie of its points, either at a fixed frame rate or as a raw point stream for playing from a laser's own SD card. Timelines export to ILDA slower than real time.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'ilda': no hits anywhere.

capability: Send laser paths to previsualisation programs and other apps
what_it_does: Laser output can be sent to 3D previsualisation software to program a show before the venue, and shared with other programs as paths over the network using the open PONK protocol. A beam preview with simulated fog can itself be shown on video outputs.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'ponk': no hits anywhere. No laser objects of any kind were found.

capability: Cue grid: snapshots of chosen parameters, each with its own transition
what_it_does: A scene stores everything; a cue stores only the parameters you click while in Edit mode. Starting a cue fades each stored parameter from its present value to the stored one, with a transition that can be set per parameter. Cues sit in a grid of banks, rows and columns; one item per row plays at a time, and launches can wait for the beat.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). pattrstorage's refpage: saves and recalls presets of client objects, with 'recall' accepting a fractional preset number for interpolation, 'recallmulti' for a weighted mix, 'interp' to set each client's interpolation mode, and 'active' and 'priority' per client. Userguide topics 'presets_and_interpolation' and 'snapshots' cover the same ground. Max can store and interpolate presets; a timed fade, per-parameter fade settings, and a grid with one-per-row playback would have to be patched.
notes: pattrstorage's 'fade' message is marked deprecated in its refpage (identical to recall).

capability: Keyframe any parameter by touching it while Record is on
what_it_does: Any cue can be given a timeline. With Record on, moving a control writes a keyframe at the playhead and adds a track for that parameter if there was none. Keyframes interpolate as steps, lines, hand-shaped Bézier curves or automatic smooth curves. Tracks can also send OSC and MIDI to other equipment.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'timeline': no Max object (package hits are Link's link.beat and link.phasor~, and bach.roll). 'keyframe': no object. mtr (refpage: records messages and plays them back in sequence) records gestures as events, not editable curves. function (refpage: breakpoint function editor, with 'setcurve') is one curve per object. jit.path and jit.anim.path interpolate between stored points. No editor that shows many parameters as tracks on one time axis was found.

capability: Master timeline that plays other timelines, with markers
what_it_does: One master timeline arranges scenes, cues and their own timelines along a time axis, next to video, audio, OSC and MIDI tracks. Expert mode lets timelines contain timelines. Playback follows its own clock, a speed control, the global BPM or an outside clock.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). transport's refpage: controls a clock for objects linked to it. timepoint: bangs when the clock reaches a time. These give a shared clock and cue points; arranging nested sequences on a visible time axis is not provided.

capability: Chase external timecode: MTC, LTC, Art-Net timecode
what_it_does: A timeline can follow timecode from outside: MIDI timecode, LTC arriving as audio, or Art-Net timecode. In expert mode different timelines can follow different sources.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'ltc', 'mtc', 'midi time code': no hits. 'smpte': only in the seq and jit.colorspace refpages. 'timecode': only dsp and adstatus text. rtin's refpage: receives MIDI real time messages; midiin: raw MIDI bytes, from which MTC could be decoded by hand. transport has a 'clocksource' attribute whose possible sources were not looked up. No LTC decoder found.
notes: Marked unsure because transport's clock sources and third-party LTC externals were not checked.

capability: Video editing tracks inside the show timeline
what_it_does: A timeline track on which movies, images and generators are cut, moved, reversed and crossfaded like in a video editor. The edited result is one media item that is assigned to surfaces, lasers or lights like any other.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). jit.playlist's refpage: organises video files as clips, each with a selected section, reorderable by dragging, with 'next', 'pause', 'selection'. That is a clip list, not clips placed at times on an axis with crossfades.

capability: Timeline markers that pause, loop or jump, with chained actions
what_it_does: Markers on a timeline decide what happens when the playhead reaches them: wait for the operator, loop back, or jump to another marker. A follow action chains a second step. Markers can be triggered by name from any controller or over OSC.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). timepoint's refpage: outputs a bang when the clock reaches a specific time. With transport that gives a cue point; the wait, loop and jump behaviour would be patched around it.

capability: Render the whole show to files: video per output, laser, DMX and audio
what_it_does: One export renders a timeline to a movie for each video output, an ILDA file for each laser, a DMX sequence and an audio mix, without having to run in real time.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). jit.record's refpage: saves a sequence of matrices as a movie, with a 'realtime' attribute. jit.vcr: the same with MSP audio. jit.gl.asyncread: reads back the GL framebuffer. The userguide has a 'Non-real-time Processing' topic with a video section, and jit.world's refpage lists 'fixed_delta'. So one video stream can be rendered offline in Max; several outputs plus laser and DMX in one pass cannot.

capability: Run shows from a calendar file or the clock
what_it_does: An exported calendar file triggers scenes and cues by event name, recurring events included. Other modules start a timeline at set times or on set weekdays, keep it running inside a daily window, start one when the project opens, or start one when nobody has touched the controls for a while.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'calendar', 'icalendar': no objects. date's refpage: reports the current date and time. A daily schedule can be patched from date; reading an .ics file with recurrence rules would need a script.

capability: Share any output with other apps: Syphon, Spout, NDI, internal loopback
what_it_does: Each output has switches to publish it to other programs on the same computer, to the network as NDI, or back into MadMapper as a live source. Incoming Syphon, Spout and NDI streams appear as media with no setup.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). Syphon: package objects jit.gl.syphonserver and jit.gl.syphonclient (Syphon package, installed). Spout: named in Vsynth's package entries as needing a Spout package that is not installed here (and is Windows only). NDI: no object in the registry, refpages or package library; the userguide 'video' topic names Syphon, Spout and OBS for recording but not NDI. Internal loopback is ordinary texture routing in Max (jit.gl.node, jit.gl.texture).
notes: NDI is the real gap on this machine.

capability: Vector media: Lottie animations and resizable SVG
what_it_does: Lottie JSON animations exported from After Effects play as media, and SVG images render at any chosen size on video surfaces or as true vectors on lasers.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'lottie': no hits anywhere. SVG: jit.mgraphics has svg_render and related methods.

capability: Depth cameras and tethered still cameras as live inputs
what_it_does: Kinect ONE and Intel RealSense depth sensors, Canon cameras through Canon's own SDK, Sony cameras and Blackmagic cards appear as live inputs, switched on in preferences.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). jit.grab's refpage: digitizes video from any digitizer; the userguide 'video_engine' topic says both platforms include native support for Blackmagic input devices. 'kinect', 'realsense', 'canon': no hits in Max or the package library.

capability: Shader whose controls are built from its own header
what_it_does: A shader file starts with a JSON block that lists its parameters. MadMapper reads it and makes the sliders, checkboxes, colour pickers and menus, grouped by label, and every one is at once available to controllers, cues and timelines. The editor recompiles as you type.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'isf': package object jit.gl.isf (package entry: renders ISF files to GL textures) is in the repo's library, but no ISF package folder was found in this machine's Packages. jit.gl.pix's refpage says it can export 'isf'. jit.gl.slab and jit.gl.shader load JXS shader files with params. jit.gl.bfg's refpage lists getparamlist, getparamtype, getparamdefault, which shows shader parameters can be enumerated; a control still has to be made for each.
notes: The gap is the automatic interface and its automatic exposure to cues and controllers, not shader loading.

capability: Smooth, tempo-aware animation values computed outside the shader
what_it_does: The shader's header can ask the host for helper values: a time that advances at a controllable speed without jumping when the speed changes, optionally locked to the beat; shaped cycles; and smoothed or eased versions of any input. They arrive as uniforms.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). Not searched as a feature: in Max these values are made in the patch and sent to the shader as params, which is more general. MadMapper is better only in that the shader file carries the request itself, so a shared shader animates correctly with no patch around it.
notes: Refpages: line generates ramps from one value to another in a set time; slide smooths a stream of values; transport runs a tempo-based clock. These are the patch-side equivalents.

capability: Audio spectrum and waveform delivered to shaders as textures
what_it_does: A shader input declared as spectrum or waveform receives a one-pixel-high texture of up to 512 values, with attack, decay and release smoothing applied to each band before the shader sees it.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). jit.catch~'s refpage: turns MSP signals into a stream of matrices, which can be sent to a shader as a texture. The FFT and the per-band smoothing are patched separately.

capability: Shader libraries for noise and 2D shapes, included by name
what_it_does: Three libraries ship with the program and are pulled into any shader with an include line: many kinds of noise in 2D and 3D with derivatives, signed-distance-field shapes with fill, stroke, glow and repetition, and colour helpers.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). jit.gl.bfg's refpage: generates textures from a library of procedural basis functions (noise, fractal, distorted) on the GPU. That gives noise as a texture source, not as functions to call inside your own shader. A package named JitLygia is in this machine's Packages folder but is not in the repo's package library and was not read.

capability: Material and effect compiled into one shader, drawn straight on the output
what_it_does: A generative material and the effect on its surface are merged into one program and drawn directly at the output's resolution, with no intermediate texture, so it stays sharp on any size of surface. A switch renders it to a fixed-size texture instead when that is cheaper or when an effect needs to sample it many times.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). jit.gl.slab processes textures stage by stage; jit.gl.shader binds one shader to geometry (refpage: compiles and submits a vertex and fragment program). Whether Max can merge two separately written shaders automatically was not found and not tested.

capability: In-app shader library: install, publish and remix community shaders
what_it_does: A panel lists shaders and effects published by other users; one click installs one into the project, and your own can be published publicly or kept private on your account. The whole library is cached for offline use.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). The userguide has a 'package_manager' topic: Max installs whole packages from inside the application. There is no per-shader library with publishing.

capability: Text prompt to a working shader with controls
what_it_does: Typing a description produces a material, laser material or 2D effect, complete with sliders for the parameters asked for; further prompts refine it, and the code stays editable. It runs on the maker's servers, one credit per prompt.
max_check: Not searched in Max: this is a paid online service, not a program feature that could be looked up as an object.
notes: Listed for completeness. The FAQ page cited was read only in its MadAI and MadLaser general sections.

capability: Map any parameter to any controller by 'learn', with range, filter and curve
what_it_does: Right-click a control or switch on Learn, move a key, MIDI control, OSC address, DMX channel, audio band or gamepad stick, and the two are linked. Each link has input and output ranges, a smoothing filter, a response curve drawn in a graph, and can send feedback to motorised or lit controllers.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). The userguide 'mapping' topic: Max's Mappings connect MIDI controllers and the computer keyboard to parameter-enabled interface objects, per patcher, with min, max, exponent, steps, relative, trigger and pickup modes; not available in Max for Live. So MIDI and key learn exist. OSC, DMX, audio and gamepad as learnable sources, filters and drawn curves were not found in that topic.

capability: Every parameter reachable by OSC without setup, and discoverable
what_it_does: Every parameter has a readable OSC address from the moment it exists, a wildcard sets many at once, and other programs can browse the whole address tree with OSCQuery. Right-clicking any control copies its address.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). Max 9 has param.osc (refpage: controls and reports parameters using OSC), osc.packet and osc.codebox, and the userguide 'OSC' topic says an OSCQuery server can be enabled in the general preferences. So Max covers this for parameter-enabled objects. Wildcard addresses were not looked for.
notes: Close to parity in Max 9. Kept in the list so the later pass can confirm what param.osc exposes.

capability: Pad controllers that mirror the cue grid, and a Stream Deck plugin
what_it_does: A Launchpad or APC shows the cue grid on its pads in each cue's colour and launches cues; the arrow keys scroll the grid. A Stream Deck key launches a cue and shows its thumbnail, and a Stream Deck+ dial turns any parameter.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'launchpad', 'apc': one package, jk.lpx (package entry: links one pad or button of a Novation Launchpad X to a live.text or live.menu, with a jk.lpxcore per patch for ports and colours). 'stream deck': no hits. So single pads can be bound; a grid that mirrors a preset bank is not provided.

capability: Switch projectors on and off and close their shutters over the network
what_it_does: A module per projector speaks PJLink: power and shutter buttons that follow the projector's real state, plus model and lamp information. Because the buttons are ordinary parameters, cues and schedulers can run a venue's projectors unattended.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'pjlink': no hits anywhere. 'tcp': Max's own hits are jit.net.send and jit.net.recv, which are for matrices; the package library has sadam.tcpClient, sadam.tcpSender, sadam.tcpReceiver and sadam.tcpServer (Sadam Library, installed). So a TCP connection is available from a package and the PJLink commands would be written by hand.
notes: The manual describes PJLink only as a network protocol; that it runs over TCP is not stated there, so sadam.tcpClient as the carrier is an assumption to confirm.

capability: Export a mapping to a small standalone player that syncs with others
what_it_does: A project's surfaces and media, or its recorded light sequences, are exported to a Raspberry Pi based box that plays them with no computer. Several boxes on one network cable keep their playback together with no configuration, and can be controlled from MadMapper or by OSC.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'raspberry': the userguide 'rnbo' topic says RNBO patchers export to hardware targets like Raspberry Pi; that is audio code, not video mapping or DMX playback. The registry has a 'standalone' object and the userguide a 'standalones_and_collectives' topic, for desktop applications.

capability: Settings for installations that run with nobody there
what_it_does: A project can open straight into fullscreen with every prompt suppressed, arm its outputs, recover from a crash using automatic saves, and be told over OSC, MIDI or DMX to quit or to shut down or restart the computer.
max_check: Searched Max 9.1.5's object registry (obj-qlookup.json), refpage names, digests and text, the userguide topics, and the repo's package library (query_packages.py). 'autosave': only pattrstorage and plug-in refpages. Max has standalones (userguide topic) and fullscreen windows; quitting or shutting down the computer by message, and crash recovery of a running patch, were not looked up.

capability: Draw order is the list order, so it is never undefined
what_it_does: Surfaces are drawn in the order of the list: the first row is in front, the last is at the back. Dragging a row changes the stacking, and there is no way for two surfaces to have an unknown order.
max_check: Read jit.group-gl.maxref.xml (the shared attributes of the jit.gl objects): 'layer' defaults to 0, rendering goes from low to high, and objects in the same layer have no guaranteed order. Read the userguide topic jitter/depth_layer_blend: every object starts in layer 0 so the order is indeterminate, higher layers draw on top, and layering only works when depth testing is off (@depth_enable 0); jit.gl.layer turns depth testing off and blending on by default.
advice: Give every overlapping plane its own @layer number and never leave two at 0. Use jit.gl.layer for flat video stacks, since it already has depth testing off. Note the direction: in Max the higher number is in front, the opposite of MadMapper's top-of-list.

capability: Levels multiply down a chain: surface, group, video master, master
what_it_does: Each surface has its own opacity. A group has one too, and the surface's value is multiplied by it. Above that sit separate masters for video, DMX, audio and laser, and one master over all of them, each multiplying what is below.
max_check: Read jit.group-gl.maxref.xml: 'color' is red green blue alpha per object, default 1 1 1 1. Read jit.gl.node's refpage: it groups child objects so they can be rendered and captured to a texture together (@capture 1); it lists no opacity of its own. Nothing in either page multiplies one object's level by a parent's.
advice: Patch the chain on purpose: each layer's alpha is its own fader times its group fader times a master, one `*` per level, with the master fader shown in the presentation. To fade a whole group at once, capture it with jit.gl.node @capture 1 and fade the one captured texture.

capability: Blend mode is a named menu on each layer, and a group keeps blending inside itself
what_it_does: Every surface has a blend mode chosen by name next to its opacity. Putting surfaces in a group keeps their blend modes and masks from affecting surfaces outside the group.
max_check: Read jit.group-gl.maxref.xml: 'blend' takes a name (add, multiply, screen, exclusion, colorblend, alphablend, coloradd, alphaadd), each equal to a 'blend_mode' pair of numbers; 'blend_enable' defaults to 0. The userguide topic jitter/depth_layer_blend says blending is off by default except on jit.gl.layer. jit.gl.node's refpage: children can be captured together to a texture.
advice: Write `@blend screen`, not `@blend_mode 4 1`, so the box says what it does, and remember `@blend_enable 1` on anything that is not a jit.gl.layer. To stop a group's blending reaching the layers under it, render the group into jit.gl.node @capture 1 and place the result as one layer.

capability: Crop the source by a rectangle first, then shape the output
what_it_does: Which part of the media a surface shows is set by a rectangle drawn over the source. Where that part lands on the projector is set separately. Changing one never disturbs the other.
max_check: Read jit.fx.subtexture's refpage (bundled Jitter Tools package): it references a sub-region of a texture without copying, with 'offset' and 'dim' in pixels. Read jit.gl.cornerpin's refpage: four corner attributes place a texture in the window. Read the Butter_tools README section on jit.butter_crop: a crop rectangle drawn on the picture passing through it; its README says the cropping inside the box has not yet been tried in Max.
advice: Keep the two steps as two objects in series: a crop (jit.fx.subtexture, or jit.butter_crop to draw it) feeding a jit.gl.cornerpin or jit.gl.meshwarp. Do not try to crop by pulling the output corners.
notes: Session 1's candidate on the surface list said Max has no input-crop view; jit.fx.subtexture supplies the crop itself, without a view.

capability: Movie loop behaviour is a named choice: loop, play once and hold, ping-pong, random frames
what_it_does: A movie's inspector has transport buttons, a playback mode chosen by name, a speed in percent, and loop in and out points that limit playback to part of the file.
max_check: Read jit.movie's refpage: 'loop' is an integer whose only described value is the default 1 (start to end); 'loopreport' mentions a palindrome mode; 'looppoints', 'loopstart', 'loopend' and 'rate' cover the in and out points and the speed. Read jit.playlist's refpage: 'loop' is on or off per clip, 'selection' sets a clip's start and end, and any jit.movie attribute can be set per clip with 'setclip'. The refpage does not list what each 'loop' number means, and holding the last frame was not found in it.
advice: Do not leave a bare number box on `loop`. Put an `attrui` on it so the mode shows its own name, and label the control with the behaviour (loop, once, back and forth). For random frames, drive the `frame` message from `random`.
notes: The meaning of each jit.movie 'loop' value should be confirmed in the help file before writing labels.

capability: One plain codec rule: HAP for scrubbing and many layers, H.264 only for straight playback
what_it_does: The manual says which codec to use for what. HAP is decoded on the graphics card and suits scrubbing, reverse and many layers, but needs a fast drive. H.264 and similar are for forward playback only; if they must be scrubbed, export them with a keyframe on every frame. It also says to add up the data rates of all clips and check the drive can deliver them.
max_check: Read the userguide topics jitter/video and jitter/video_engine: both video engines play HAP natively; the video page suggests HAP, or loading the file into memory, for random access and resequencing. The bundled 'hap' package describes itself as a HAP video engine for efficient realtime playback. Max's pages give no keyframe or drive-speed advice.
advice: Same rule in Max: transcode to HAP anything that is scrubbed, reversed, retriggered or layered. If a file must stay H.264, export it all-intra. Check the drive's read speed against the sum of the clips playing at once.

capability: The manual says when hardware decoding breaks audio routing
what_it_does: On macOS, hardware decoding of H.264 and HEVC sends the movie's sound to the system's default output and ignores the program's own audio settings. The manual says so and recommends leaving it off when the sound matters.
max_check: Read the userguide topic jitter/video: jit.movie plays audio directly through the video engine, not through Max; jit.movie~ brings the audio tracks into MSP, and mc.jit.movie~ gives them as multichannel audio. jit.movie~'s refpage (bundled VIDDLL package): plays a movie and routes its audio into MSP.
advice: When a movie's sound has to pass through the patch, for a level, a mute, an effect or a chosen output, use jit.movie~ and not jit.movie. With jit.movie the sound goes out of the computer without ever reaching a cord.

capability: A movie's sound level can follow its layer's opacity
what_it_does: A switch on each movie ties its audio level to the opacity of the surface it is on, so fading the picture fades the sound. The FAQ gives this as the way to fade audio between cues.
max_check: Read jit.movie's refpage: 'vol' is the movie sound volume. No attribute links it to any drawing object's colour or alpha.
advice: Send one fader to both places: the layer's alpha and the movie's `vol` (or a `live.gain~` after jit.movie~). A video crossfade that leaves the old clip's sound at full level is the usual result of forgetting this.

capability: A folder of numbered stills plays as a movie, with frame rate, cache and auto scan
what_it_does: A folder of numbered images is one media item that plays like a movie. It has its own frames per second, a setting for how many frames to preload, the same loop modes as movies, and it picks up files added to the folder while running.
max_check: Read jit.gl.textureset's refpage (bundled Jitter Tools package): it keeps a set of textures for storage and resequencing, written by 'index' and read with 'outputtexture', the texture version of jit.matrixset. jit.movie's refpage has nothing about image sequences. No object that takes a folder and plays it was found; a folder-watching object was not searched for.
advice: For a short sequence, load the frames into jit.gl.textureset once and step through them with a counter at the wanted rate. For a long one, turn the stills into a HAP movie first; that is less patching and plays better.

capability: Shader drawn once at a set size, or drawn per surface at output resolution: the user chooses
what_it_does: The same shader can run two ways. As a Generator it is rendered once into a texture of a size you type in, and every surface using it shares that picture. As a Material it is rendered again on each surface, at the projector's resolution, which is sharper and costs more. Dragging a Material into the Generators list switches it.
max_check: Read jit.gl.slab's refpage: it renders a shader into a texture; 'adapt' (default 1) takes the size from the input, and 'dim' (default 256 256) is used when adapt is off; 'dimscale' scales the output. Read jit.gl.shader's refpage: it compiles a shader and binds it to an object, so it is drawn with that object's geometry. jit.gl.pix's refpage calls it essentially a jit.gl.slab whose shader comes from a Gen patcher.
advice: Make the choice on purpose. Give a shader that has no input an explicit size, `@adapt 0 @dim <w> <h>`: the refpage only defines the output size for that case, and its default is 256 x 256. Use the slab (one render, shared by every plane) for heavy shaders shown in several places, and jit.gl.shader on the plane itself when one surface must stay sharp at any size.

capability: Changing a layer's media crossfades; changing its effect cannot
what_it_does: When a cue with a fade time swaps the media on a surface, MadMapper draws the surface twice during the fade, old media and new, at changing opacity. It does not do this for effects: a different effect just switches, and the FAQ says to use two surfaces to fade between effects.
max_check: Read jit.fx.tr.xfade's refpage (bundled Jitter Tools package): a crossfade between two textures set by 'xfade', 0 to 1. The same folder holds other transitions (jit.fx.tr.dissolve, slide, gridwipe, zoomfade and more). jit.xfade's registry digest: crossfade between two matrices. jit.playlist's refpage shows no crossfade between clips.
advice: Build clip changes as A/B: two players into jit.fx.tr.xfade, a `line` on `xfade`, and load the next clip into whichever side is at zero. Fading between two effect chains works the same way in Max, which MadMapper cannot do on one surface.

capability: A warp grid with masks, undo and its own save file (Max has one: jit.gl.meshwarp)
what_it_does: A surface can be given a grid of warp points. Points are added one at a time or by subdivision, each can have Bézier handles, masks can be drawn on the same surface, and by default the input mesh follows the output mesh so the picture is not stretched.
max_check: Read jit.gl.meshwarp's refpage in the bundled Jitter Tools package (it is not in the main obj-qlookup.json, which is why session 1's search for 'warp' found no object): a draggable mesh set by 'meshdim', curvature through 'nurbs_order' / 'curvature', a 'mask_mode' for drawing masks with 'invert_mask' and 'apply_mask', 'save' and 'read' of the whole state as a JSON file, undo and redo, 'layer', and 'output_texture'. It lists no free-placed points, per-point Bézier handles, linked input mesh or feathering.
advice: Reach for jit.gl.meshwarp before building a warp editor. Save its state with `save` to a JSON file beside the patch and `read` it at load: a warp is calibration for one room, so it belongs in its own file, not in the piece's presets.
notes: Corrects session 1's candidate 'Mesh warping with free points, Bézier handles and a linked input mesh', whose Max check did not find this object.

capability: The mapping stage is kept apart from the content and locked for the show
what_it_does: The manual's advice for anything beyond one projector: compose the content on an off-screen buffer, publish it as a loopback, and map that one source onto the projectors. Cues then change the content and never touch the projector mapping. Surfaces and outputs can be locked against accidental edits.
max_check: Read jit.world's refpage: 'output_texture' captures the scene to a texture and 'enable_cornerpin' shows an internal cornerpin. Read jit.gl.cornerpin's refpage: 'enable_mouse' and 'drawcorners' turn the handles off. jit.gl.meshwarp's refpage has 'show_ui'. The repo's own table (CLAUDE.md, Preferred Objects) already recommends a first jit.world captured to a texture and a second stage that maps it.
advice: Build two stages: everything creative renders into one texture, and a separate mapping stage places that texture. Give the mapping stage one 'calibrate' toggle that sets `enable_mouse` and `drawcorners` (or `show_ui`), off by default, so a stray click during the show cannot move a corner.

capability: Corner and warp points can be moved from the keyboard
what_it_does: Tab steps to the next corner handle. The arrow keys move the selected point by one pixel, and by ten with Shift. The manual says the mouse is too coarse for the last few pixels of an alignment.
max_check: Read jit.gl.cornerpin's refpage: corners move by mouse in the window or by setting 'upper_left', 'upper_right', 'lower_left', 'lower_right'; it lists no keyboard control. jit.gl.meshwarp's refpage lists keyboard shortcuts for undo and redo only. key's refpage: reports key presses, no inlets.
advice: Add a small nudge patch to any cornerpin: `key` picks the corner (or Tab cycles), the arrows add or subtract one pixel's worth (1 / window width) to that corner's attribute, Shift makes it ten. It is a handful of objects and saves real time in front of a projector.

capability: Each output knows its display; fullscreen is one switch for all of them
what_it_does: An output has a Destination menu naming a real display, a size that can be copied from that display, and its own Desktop Window button. One command sends every output fullscreen on its display and another brings them back. The project can be set to open fullscreen. The FAQ lists the system settings that break this: mirrored displays, and a maximised interface window on macOS.
max_check: Read jit.world's and jit.window's refpages: 'fullscreen', 'fsmenubar', 'rect', 'windowposition' / 'pos', 'size', 'border' and 'floating' are separate attributes; neither has an attribute that names a display. Read jit.displays' refpage: 'count' and 'coords <index>' report each display's rectangle, and on Mac it can mirror and unmirror. Which display a fullscreen window lands on is not stated in the refpages.
advice: Do in the patch what MadMapper does in its menu: at load, ask jit.displays for the projector display's coords, move the window there with `rect`, then set `fullscreen 1`, all from one 'show' toggle that drives every jit.world. Check for mirroring first and tell the operator if it is on.
notes: That a Max window goes fullscreen on the display it sits on is the common practice, but it was not confirmed in a refpage here.

capability: Each output has a frame delay to line up slow and fast projectors
what_it_does: Every video output has a delay, counted in frames, so a fast display can be held back to match a slower projector in the same setup.
max_check: Read jit.fx.delay's refpage (bundled Jitter Tools package): delays a texture by 'delay' frames, up to 'max_delay' (default 30), with 'interp' (default 1) blending between the current and the delayed frame.
advice: Put jit.fx.delay on the texture going to the faster display and set `@interp 0` so frames are delayed, not blended. One object per output, placed in the mapping stage.

capability: The engine's frame rate is a project setting
what_it_does: The frame rate of the whole engine is either left on Auto, following the display, or set to a fixed number in the project's preferences. The FAQ uses it to limit the rate of an NDI output.
max_check: Read jit.world's refpage: 'fps' and 'interval' only take effect when 'enable' is 1 and 'displaylink' is 0; 'displaylink' (default 1, Mac only) ties drawing to the display's refresh; 'sync' is vertical sync; 'running_fps' reports the real rate.
advice: On a Mac, `@fps` does nothing until `@displaylink 0` is also set. Decide per patch whether the display or a number sets the rate, write both attributes on the jit.world, and show `running_fps` somewhere the operator can see.

capability: One master speed and one freeze act on everything that moves
what_it_does: Master Settings has a speed that scales every animated thing at once, shaders and audio included, a Freeze Engine that stops it all, and a Freeze Video Output that holds the picture while playback carries on underneath. Shaders that must ignore the speed read wall-clock time instead.
max_check: Read jit.mo.time's refpage (bundled jit.mo package): outputs accumulated time, frame delta or a function, in step with jit.world, with a 'speed' multiplier and an 'interval' in Max time format. transport's refpage: one tempo for everything tempo-relative. jit.world's 'enable' stops all rendering. Nothing found scales every animation in a patch at once.
advice: Give a patch one time source: a single jit.mo.time (or the transport) whose output every shader and animation reads, with one speed control in front of it. Then 'slow everything down' and 'freeze' are one control each instead of a hunt through the patch.
notes: How to hold the last rendered frame in Max while the scene keeps running was not looked up.

capability: Global tempo has a source menu: audio beat detection, Ableton Link, MIDI clock, manual and tap
what_it_does: One tempo drives everything tempo-aware. Its source is picked from a menu: detected from the audio input, Ableton Link, MIDI clock, or typed and tapped by hand. There is a Resync button. The FAQ notes that animations stop when the tempo is zero or its source is disconnected.
max_check: Read transport's refpage: 'tempo', and 'clocksource' with a 'getclocksources' message that lists the active sources at run time; the page does not name them. The installed Link package has link.session (start, stop and tempo of the shared session), link.beat and link.phasor~ refpages, and an extensions folder holding link.clocksource. The package library lists pnp.bpm~ as a tempo estimator. No tap-tempo object was found.
advice: Keep one `transport` as the only tempo in the patch and feed it from a single selector (a `umenu` of sources). Read `getclocksources` to see what this machine offers. Show the tempo and warn when it is 0, because everything written in note values stops with it.
notes: Settles part of session 1's open question: transport's sources are reported by getclocksources, and Link ships a clock source extension. The source names were not read, since that needs Max running.

capability: Audio analysis arrives as a few named channels: amplitude, bass, medium, treble, beat counts
what_it_does: The audio input is analysed once, on channels chosen in the preferences, and offered everywhere as named values. Any slider can be tied to one from its right-click menu.
max_check: Read the refpages: peakamp~ reports a signal's peak amplitude; fffb~ is a fixed bank of bandpass filters with one outlet per band; snapshot~ turns a signal into numbers at an interval; slide smooths a stream of values. Max has far more analysis than MadMapper, but nothing arrives pre-named.
advice: Build the analysis once, in one place: input, a three-band split, an envelope per band, then `s AMP`, `s BASS`, `s MID`, `s TREBLE`. Every visual reads those names. Analysing the same input separately beside each effect is the usual Max mistake this avoids.

capability: Two ways in for every parameter: a direct address for the raw value, a mapped Control for range, filter and curve
what_it_does: Every parameter has a fixed OSC address built from the names of things in the project, such as /surfaces/Quad-1/opacity. A value sent there is applied as it is. A Control mapped to the same parameter adds a source range, a target range, a filter and a curve. Renaming a surface changes its address.
max_check: Read the userguide topic OSC: with OSC enabled, parameter-enabled objects get addresses of the form /<patcher name>/param/<parameter name>, with /raw and /normalized under each; OSCQuery can be switched on in the preferences. Read param.osc's refpage: 'info' and 'allparams' output every parameter's details and values as OSC. Wildcards in addresses, which MadMapper accepts, are not mentioned in either.
advice: Treat patcher names and parameter names as a public interface: choose them before giving addresses to anyone, because a rename breaks every remote. Send 0 to 1 to /normalized from generic controllers and real units to /raw from show control. In a hand-built patch, give a parameter the same two entries: a plain set, and a scaled and smoothed one.

capability: Controllers get the current values sent back
what_it_does: Each MIDI input can be paired with a feedback device, and OSC has a feedback port and address. When a value changes inside MadMapper, motor faders, button lights and tablet layouts are updated to match.
max_check: Read the userguide topic mapping: if Map is enabled for a MIDI output port, every MIDI-mapped interface object sends its control change or note to that port with no midiout object. Read param.osc's refpage: 'auto' reports parameter changes as OSC, and 'set' dispatches incoming OSC to parameters without triggering output. udpsend's refpage: sends messages and OSC packets to a host and port.
advice: Turn on Map for the controller's output port in MIDI Setup; that is the whole of MIDI feedback. For a tablet, `param.osc @auto 1` into `udpsend`, and bring incoming values in through its `set` message so they are not echoed straight back.
notes: Max is level with MadMapper here; the Max feature is easy to miss because it lives in the MIDI Setup window.

capability: A preset shows when the live values no longer match what it stored
what_it_does: After a cue is recalled and then changed by hand, the changed controls are outlined, so the operator can see the cue is no longer what is on stage. One command writes the live values back into the cue, and several cues can be updated at once.
max_check: Read pattrstorage's refpage: 'getedited' reports 1 when the data of the current preset has been edited, 'getcurrent' reports the active preset, 'storeagain' stores into the last-used slot, and 'lock' protects a slot from being overwritten. Nothing marks which control changed.
advice: Poll `getedited` after any change and light one indicator beside the preset control; put an 'Update' button on `storeagain`. Lock finished presets so a stray store cannot overwrite them.

capability: Presets leave playing media alone unless told to restart it
what_it_does: A Scene stores everything and so tends to restart media when recalled; the manual warns about this and steers operators to Cues, which store only chosen parameters. The FAQ's fix for audio that restarts on a cue is to untick the player's Replay value inside that cue.
max_check: Read pattrstorage's refpage: 'active <client> 0' leaves a client out of every recall; 'subscribemode' with 'subscribe' makes the object manage only a listed set of clients; 'priority' sets the order clients are restored in.
advice: Decide which controls are state and which are actions. Leave play, restart and file-load controls out of pattrstorage (`active <name> 0`, or `@subscribemode 1` with an explicit list), or every preset recall will restart the clips. Use one pattrstorage per concern (looks, media, mix) the way MadMapper uses one row per concern.

capability: A project is a folder, and one command collects every outside file into it
what_it_does: A project is a folder holding the project files, auto-saves and a resources folder. Collect External Resources copies every referenced movie, sound and image into it, so the folder can be moved to the show computer or archived whole.
max_check: Read the userguide topic projects: a Max Project collects patchers, media, code and externals, is saved automatically, and puts its own files ahead of the global search path. Manage Project offers Consolidate (copy all dependencies into the project folder) and Archive (one .maxzip file). Whether a media file named only inside a message box counts as a dependency was not checked.
advice: For anything that will run on another machine, save it as a Project and Consolidate before moving it. Keep media in the project folder and load it by file name, not by an absolute path, so the copy still finds it.

capability: Settings are split in two: this computer, and this project
what_it_does: Preferences have two tabs. Application holds what belongs to the machine: audio device, capture devices, graphics options. Project holds what belongs to the piece and travels with it: MIDI devices, OSC ports, DMX routing, engine frame rate, whether to open fullscreen.
max_check: Read the userguide topic OSC: the UDP server is switched on either for the whole application in the preferences or for one patcher in the patcher inspector. The video_engine topic: the video engine is an application preference that an object can override with @engine. The mapping topic: mappings belong to a patcher. So Max has both levels, but a patch's own machine choices (which display, which port, which camera) have no set home.
advice: Keep machine-specific choices out of the piece's presets. Put display index, audio device, MIDI port names and camera names in one small config file (a `dict` read at load) so that moving to another computer means editing one file, and the presets stay about the piece.

capability: Saving during a show is treated as a risk: a countdown, a pause button, and rotating backups
what_it_does: AutoSave writes recovery files, never over the project itself, and shows a ten-second countdown first so a performer can cancel it; the manual gives a drop in frame rate during the save as one reason. A toolbar button pauses it until quit. Each manual save keeps the previous version, up to a set number.
max_check: Read pattrstorage's refpage: 'savemode' chooses between prompting and saving the preset file automatically when the patcher is saved or freed; 'backupmode' keeps a set number of rotating backup files. The userguide says projects are saved automatically, and a page on messages to Max mentions crash recovery as a Max preference.
advice: Set `@backupmode` on pattrstorage so a bad store during rehearsal can be undone from the previous file. Do not write files while performing: trigger preset saves from an explicit button used between pieces, not from a timer.

capability: Sources that are not on screen stop working unless marked 'keep running'
what_it_does: A network video source is only processed while a visible surface uses it; a tick box keeps it running in the background for instant availability, and is labelled as costing more. The media preview and the two editing views can be switched off to save rendering.
max_check: Read the refpages: jit.movie has 'start' and 'stop'; jit.grab has 'open' and 'close'; the shared jit.gl attribute 'enable' turns an object's drawing off; the jit.fx objects have 'enable' and 'bypass'. Nothing stops a source by itself when its layer becomes invisible.
advice: When a layer's opacity reaches 0, also stop what feeds it: `stop` the movie, `enable 0` on its effects. Where an instant return matters more than the cost, leave it running and say so in a comment. Give every preview a toggle; a preview is a second render.

capability: Hover help: a status line explains whatever is under the mouse
what_it_does: A line at the bottom of the window describes the control the mouse is over, for every control in the program.
max_check: Read the userguide topic objects, section Annotations and Hints: @annotation sets the text the Clue bar shows when hovering over an object, and @hint adds a pop-up that appears only when the patcher is locked.
advice: Give every presentation control a `hint`. It costs one attribute per control and is the only documentation an operator sees in the middle of a show.

capability: An LFO is a ready-made module: shape, free or tempo-synced, speed, phase, range, and a bank of ten with spread
what_it_does: An Oscillator module outputs a value between 0 and 1 with a chosen wave shape, running at a set speed or locked to the tempo, with phase and range. The 2D version gives two related values; the Bank gives ten whose phases are spread by one Offset control. Any parameter can take one as its control.
max_check: Read jit.mo.time's refpage (bundled jit.mo package): in 'mode function' it outputs line, sin, saw or perlin values in step with the render context, with 'freq', 'phase', 'speed', 'scale', 'offset', and an 'interval' in Max time format so it can be tempo-relative. Read jit.mo.func's refpage: the same functions spread across the cells of a matrix, with 'freq' and 'phase', which gives many phase-offset values at once.
advice: For values that drive visuals, use jit.mo.time @mode function; it ticks with the render, so there is no metro to keep in step. Its `interval` takes Max time values, so a note value locks it to the transport's tempo. For a spread of related values, read them from one jit.mo.func matrix.

capability: Mixing two control sources on one parameter is done by a module that says how
what_it_does: A parameter takes one Control per kind of source. To let several inputs act on it, a Controls Combiner module mixes them using a chosen combination mode. A Macro module does the reverse: one widget that many Controls point at.
max_check: Read maximum's refpage: outputs the greater of the incoming value and its stored one. In Max several message cords into one inlet do not combine: each message simply replaces the last (the repo's CLAUDE.md notes that only signal cords sum). So Max allows any number of sources, which MadMapper does not, but states no rule for how they meet.
advice: When two things drive one parameter, an LFO and a fader, audio and a preset, put the rule in the patch as a visible object: `maximum`, `*` or `+`. Two cords into one inlet is 'last one wins', and it looks deliberate when it is not.
notes: The combination modes the Controls Combiner offers are not listed in the documents read.

capability: Two clips kept frame-locked by putting them side by side in one file
what_it_does: The documented way to keep two videos in step is to make one wide file with both side by side, then let two surfaces each crop their half. One decoder cannot drift from itself.
max_check: Read jit.fx.subtexture's refpage: a sub-region of a texture by 'offset' and 'dim', without copying. jit.movie's refpage offers 'time' and 'frame' for seeking but nothing that slaves one movie to another.
advice: For clips that must stay in step, including one picture split across projectors, play one wide movie and cut it with jit.fx.subtexture. Do not start two jit.movie objects together and hope.
notes: Not tested in Max; the reasoning is MadMapper's, applied to Max objects whose refpages were read.

capability: Game controllers arrive with named buttons, sticks and triggers
what_it_does: PlayStation and Xbox controllers and generic USB HID devices are control sources. Their inputs are offered by name, and each mapping has the same range, filter, curve and toggle settings as any other Control.
max_check: Read gamepad's refpage: reports button, joystick, trigger and sensor events from all connected controllers through the SDL library's mapped names, can load extra controller mappings, and sends rumble and LED colour back with 'senddevice'. The registry digest for hi calls it legacy.
advice: Use `gamepad`, not `hi`, for controllers: the inputs come out already named, and it can drive rumble and the light bar, which MadMapper's page does not offer.
notes: Max is at least level here.
